scenes.narration: AI has never seen your company files.
Welcome to FredsDesk, lesson forty-four. In one minute, you'll learn how AI answers questions about documents it was never trained on.
The trick is called RAG: retrieval-augmented generation. In plain English: look up the right facts first, then let the AI answer using them.
scenes.definition: Look up the right facts first, then let the AI answer using them.

scenes.narration: First, your documents are turned into numbers called embeddings. Pieces with similar meaning land close together. When you ask a question, it becomes a point too, and the closest pieces are retrieved.
Then the pipeline runs in four steps. Your question goes in. The system searches your documents. The best matches are added to the prompt. And the AI writes an answer grounded in them.
Quick recap. One: RAG looks things up before answering. Two: similar meaning means close together. Three: the answer is grounded in your own documents.
Quiz time! What does the R in RAG stand for: A, retrieval, or B, reasoning? Answer in the comments. Tomorrow: how AI splits documents into chunks. Follow FredsDesk, and see you at the desk.
scenes.question: What does the R in RAG stand for?
